title: Cost review: supplier invoice payment
executiveSummary:
The process pays invoices correctly but spends most of its effort on work that adds no value: typing invoice data, chasing purchase order numbers and waiting for approvals by e-mail.
- About 50 hours a month go into manual data entry alone (600 invoices at 5 minutes each).
- Approvals take three days on average and caused late fees twice last quarter.
- Two duplicate payments were found last year because the duplicate check depends on exact typing.
Capturing invoices automatically and moving approvals into the ERP would remove most of this cost within a few months.

score.label: Significant savings available
score.rationale: Twelve of fourteen activities are manual, one invoice in five needs rework to find its purchase order, and the slowest step has no system support.

dimensions.name: Manual effort
dimensions.comment: Data entry, matching and reconciliation are all done by hand.

dimensions.name: Rework and errors
dimensions.comment: Missing purchase orders and mismatches send invoices back; duplicates slip through.

dimensions.name: Hand-offs and waiting
dimensions.comment: Seven hand-offs; approvals wait three days on average.

dimensions.name: Automation level
dimensions.comment: The ERP is used as a register, not as a workflow.

dimensions.name: Control overhead
dimensions.comment: The dual authorisation at the bank is proportionate.

findings.title: Invoice data is typed into the ERP by hand
findings.description: Every invoice is opened and its supplier, amount, due date and purchase order number are keyed in manually.
findings.evidence: "I open each one and type the data into the ERP by hand ... about five minutes per invoice, and we get roughly 600 a month." (Paulo, 00:31)
findings.impact: Roughly 50 hours of clerical work a month, plus typing errors that defeat the duplicate check.
findings.recommendation: Introduce invoice capture (e-invoice import or OCR) so accounts payable only reviews exceptions. Owner: AP manager.

findings.title: Approvals by e-mail are slow and cause late fees
findings.description: Approvers reply by e-mail, by phone or in the corridor. Nothing reminds them and nobody can see what is pending.
findings.evidence: "Three days on average, and if the manager is travelling it can be more than a week. We paid late fees twice last quarter." (Carla, 02:26)
findings.impact: Late fees, lost early-payment discounts and time spent chasing approvers.
findings.recommendation: Use the ERP approval workflow with mobile approval, automatic reminders after 24 hours and a named deputy for each cost centre.

findings.title: One invoice in five arrives without a purchase order
findings.description: Accounts payable has to find out who ordered and wait for the purchase order number before the invoice can be matched.
findings.evidence: "Then I e-mail the person who ordered it and wait. That can take days. About one in five invoices comes without a PO." (Paulo, 00:58)
findings.impact: About 120 invoices a month are handled twice and wait days before matching can start.
findings.recommendation: Adopt a "no PO, no pay" rule with suppliers and reject invoices without a purchase order at the source.

findings.title: Duplicate payments are not reliably prevented
findings.description: The duplicate check compares invoice numbers exactly as typed, so a small typing difference lets a duplicate through.
findings.evidence: "If the number is typed slightly differently it goes through. We found two duplicate payments last year." (Paulo, 03:54)
findings.impact: Cash paid twice and effort to recover it. The amounts were not stated.
findings.recommendation: Add a fuzzy duplicate check on supplier, amount and date before each payment run.

findings.title: Bank reconciliation is done in a spreadsheet
findings.description: Treasury downloads the statement, reconciles it in a spreadsheet and then marks each invoice as paid in the ERP.
findings.evidence: "That reconciliation is manual and takes me about two hours each time." (Rui, 03:28)
findings.impact: About 16 hours a month of treasury time.
findings.recommendation: Import the bank statement into the ERP and let it clear paid invoices automatically.

sections.body: The table lists the steps where effort or money is lost, from the largest driver to the smallest.

sections.heading: Quick wins and structural changes
sections.body:
Within weeks, with what already exists:
- Name a deputy approver for every cost centre.
- Send suppliers a notice that invoices need a purchase order number.
- Run a duplicate report on supplier, amount and date before each payment run.
Needing investment:
- Invoice capture and automatic three-way matching.
- Approval workflow in the ERP.
- Automatic bank statement import.

sections.heading: Savings estimate and assumptions
sections.body: The sources give volumes and durations for data entry and reconciliation, which together account for about 66 hours a month. They do not give hourly cost, the value of late fees or of the duplicate payments, so no monetary saving is stated here. To size it, collect: the loaded hourly cost of accounts payable and treasury, late fees paid in the last twelve months, early-payment discounts missed, and the value of the duplicates found.

actions.title: Name deputy approvers
actions.description: One deputy per cost centre, with the same limit.

actions.title: Enforce purchase orders with suppliers
actions.description: Communicate the rule and reject invoices without a PO.

actions.title: Add a pre-payment duplicate check
actions.description: Report on supplier, amount and date before each run.

actions.title: Move approvals into the ERP workflow
actions.description: Mobile approval, reminders and an audit trail.

actions.title: Automate invoice capture and matching
actions.description: E-invoice import or OCR with automatic three-way match.

actions.title: Import bank statements automatically
actions.description: Clear paid invoices in the ERP without the spreadsheet.

openQuestions: What is the loaded hourly cost of the accounts payable and treasury staff?
How much was paid in late fees in the last twelve months?
Which share of suppliers can send structured e-invoices?
limitations: The meeting gave no monetary values, so savings are expressed in hours. Volumes and durations are the participants' estimates and were not measured.
